main.title: The Elder Scrolls Online
main.subtitle: Explore Tamriel alone or alongside other adventurers
main.summary: The Elder Scrolls Online brought a series associated with solitary journeys into a world shared with other players.

cards.heading: Tamriel becomes a shared online world
cards.text: The Elder Scrolls Online is ZeniMax Online Studios' multiplayer role-playing game, launched for PC and Mac on 4 April 2014. Tamriel becomes a shared world in which players can follow quests alone, explore with friends or join large battles against other players. The familiar setting accommodates individual journeys alongside encounters with other adventurers.

cards.heading: Solo quests, small groups and large battles
cards.text: The available activities support different sizes of group. A player can pursue a quest alone, travel with a few companions or take part in a battle involving hundreds of participants. Moving between those activities changes who shares the encounter and what the group is trying to achieve, while keeping the journey within Tamriel.

cards.heading: The scale of the original launch
cards.text: Bethesda reported five million beta registrations before launch, reflecting the interest gathered during testing. The release introduced that audience to a shared version of a setting associated with earlier Elder Scrolls adventures. PlayStation 4 and Xbox One versions were still in development when the PC and Mac game opened in April 2014.

cards.heading: Seven years of development at ZeniMax Online
cards.text: The Elder Scrolls Online had been in development for seven years before its release in 2014. It was the first project from ZeniMax Online Studios, which was formed in 2007 as a subsidiary of ZeniMax Media. Matt Firor, studio lead at ZeniMax Online, served as director of The Elder Scrolls Online. ZeniMax Online licensed the HeroEngine in November 2007, which was used as a whiteboard for the game while the main production engine was in development. The game's development was funded by Providence Equity Partners and reinvested profits from the success of The Elder Scrolls IV: Oblivion.

main.title: Trials Fusion
main.subtitle: Balance a motorcycle across futuristic obstacle courses
main.summary: Trials Fusion is a platform racing video game developed by Ubisoft RedLynx in collaboration with Ubisoft Shanghai and Ubisoft Kyiv. A follow-up to Trials Evolution, it is the fifth game in the Trials series and is the first one to be released on a PlayStation platform. The game was released on Microsoft Windows, PlayStation 4, Xbox 360 and Xbox One in April 2014. A companion game, Trials Frontier, was released on iOS and Android devices and designed to accompany the console and PC title. Ubisoft released six paid DLC packs, as well as several free content updates. Online multiplayer was added in an update on January 24, 2015.

cards.heading: Trials reaches PlayStation with a futuristic racing setting
cards.text: Trials Fusion is RedLynx's 2014 motorcycle obstacle-course game, developed with Ubisoft Shanghai and Ubisoft Kyiv. The fifth Trials entry followed Trials Evolution onto Windows, Xbox 360 and Xbox One, and brought the series to PlayStation 4. Players balance a rider through futuristic courses, controlling acceleration and body position to clear obstacles and land safely. A track editor lets them build further challenges, while later updates expanded the multiplayer options.

cards.heading: Weight shifts, aerial tricks and different vehicles
cards.text: The motorcycle travels along a two-dimensional route through a three-dimensional setting. Leaning changes its balance: the rider shifts weight to lift a wheel, negotiate an obstacle or bring the bike into position before landing. A badly judged movement can undo a successful jump. Fusion adds freestyle motocross tricks controlled with the right stick during flight, giving the player another task before touching down. Courses grow more demanding as the game progresses, and selected stages introduce other vehicles, including the TKO Panda quad bike.

cards.heading: Build tracks and race against other players
cards.text:
Trials Fusion also features a track editor, allowing players to create their own courses and games.

Trials Fusion's multiplayer allows up to 8 players (PS4, Xbox One and PC) to race in different tracks, while the Xbox 360 version of the game only supports 4 players. Online multiplayer was added in an update on January 24, 2015.

main.title: Child of Light
main.subtitle: Help Aurora restore the lights of Lemuria
main.summary: Child of Light is a platforming role-playing video game developed by Ubisoft Montreal and published by Ubisoft for Windows, PlayStation 3, PlayStation 4, Wii U, Xbox 360 and Xbox One in April 2014, and was released on PlayStation Vita in July 2014.

cards.heading: A role-playing adventure built with UbiArt
cards.text: Child of Light is Ubisoft Montreal's 2014 role-playing adventure, built with the UbiArt Framework. Aurora explores the land of Lemuria through side-scrolling landscapes, meeting companions and entering battles governed by a turn-based timing system. Two party members fight at a time and can be exchanged for waiting allies. The game first appeared on Windows and home consoles before reaching PlayStation Vita and, later, Nintendo Switch.

cards.heading: Aurora and the light of Igniculus
cards.text: Aurora wakes in Lemuria and must recover the sun, moon and stars from the Queen of the Night to find a way home. The firefly Igniculus accompanies her. Moving his light reaches chests Aurora cannot access and helps during combat: shining on an enemy slows it, while lighting an ally restores health. Approaching an opponent from behind also gives the party an opening advantage. Exploration and battle both make use of how the player directs this small companion.

cards.heading: Reception of the illustrated adventure
cards.text: The watercolour-inspired setting, character designs and Cœur de pirate's piano score received praise alongside the battle system. Reviews also found points of friction: the rhyming dialogue could feel forced, and some considered the challenge and character upgrades too slight. Igniculus drew particular attention because moving his light adds a direct action to battles organised around turns. The reception reflected both the illustrated presentation and the decisions available within it.

main.title: Bound by Flame
main.subtitle: Choose between demonic power and human resolve
main.summary: Bound by Flame is a 2014 action role-playing game developed by Spiders and published by Focus Home Interactive. Bound by Flame puts the player in the role of a victim of demonic possession who must choose between the evil powers that are offered or rejecting them in favor of developing heroic talents.

cards.heading: A mercenary caught between human resolve and demonic power
cards.text: Bound by Flame is a 2014 action role-playing game developed by Spiders and published by Focus Home Interactive. Bound by Flame puts the player in the role of a victim of demonic possession who must choose between the evil powers that are offered or rejecting them in favor of developing heroic talents.

cards.heading: Companions and choices shape the journey
cards.text: Through its different chapters, Bound by Flame follows a main quest with optional side quests. Several companions will join the player during their quest, and will, depending on the player's actions, develop friendship, romance, or rivalry. Depending on the choices made by the player and the influence of the demon, some chapters will offer different scenarios and a different experience.

cards.heading: Three skill trees offer different approaches to combat
cards.text: The player can choose between three different skill trees that affect combat abilities; Ranger, Pyromancer, and Warrior. The Warrior skill tree relies on slow, heavy, strikes with large weapons, and a push/kick ability to interrupt enemies or break their defences. The Ranger skill tree uses small weapons like daggers for quick strikes and gives a dodge ability to evade enemy attacks. The Pyromancer skill tree utilizes high damage fire attacks which can be combined with the Ranger and Warrior skill trees to do things like enhance weapons with fire damage.

main.title: Wolfenstein: The New Order
main.subtitle: B.J. Blazkowicz fights through an alternate 1960s Europe
main.summary: Wolfenstein: The New Order is a 2014 first-person shooter game developed by MachineGames and published by Bethesda Softworks.

cards.heading: Resistance in a Europe ruled by the Nazis
cards.text: Wolfenstein: The New Order is a 2014 first-person shooter game developed by MachineGames and published by Bethesda Softworks. It was released on 20 May 2014 for PlayStation 3, PlayStation 4, Windows, Xbox 360, and Xbox One. The game is the sixth main entry in the Wolfenstein series and the first since 2009's Wolfenstein. Set in an alternate history 1960s Europe where the Nazis won the Second World War, the story follows war veteran William "B.J." Blazkowicz and his efforts to stop the Nazis from ruling over the world.

cards.heading: Chapter choices, weapons and dual wielding
cards.text: The game is played from a first-person perspective and most of its levels are navigated on foot. The story is arranged in chapters, which players complete in order to progress. A morality choice in the prologue alters the game's storyline; some characters and small plot points are replaced throughout the two timelines. The game features a variety of weapons, most of which can be dual wielded. A cover system is present.

cards.heading: MachineGames develops Blazkowicz as a character
cards.text: MachineGames began work in 2010, building on the series' combat and adventure elements while giving Blazkowicz a larger dramatic role. The team wanted players to become interested in the man carrying the weapons as well as the action around him. That emphasis placed character development alongside the alternate-history setting, giving the resistance campaign a personal perspective through its returning protagonist.

cards.heading: Critical reception and the later series
cards.text: At release, Wolfenstein: The New Order received generally positive reviews, with praise particularly directed at the combat and the narrative of the game. Critics considered it a positive change to the series and nominated it for multiple year-end accolades, including Game of the Year and Best Shooter awards from several gaming publications. A stand-alone expansion, Wolfenstein: The Old Blood, was released in May 2015 and is set before the events of the game. A sequel, Wolfenstein II: The New Colossus, was released in October 2017.

main.title: Transistor
main.subtitle: Combine Functions and plan Red’s battles through Cloudbank
main.summary: Transistor is an action role-playing game developed and published by Supergiant Games.

cards.heading: Supergiant releases its second game
cards.text: Transistor is Supergiant Games' 2014 action role-playing game, first released for Windows and PlayStation 4. Red, a singer in the city of Cloudbank, carries a greatsword-like weapon into battles against robotic enemies called the Process. Fighting moves between real-time action and a frozen planning mode, while the weapon's Functions can be combined as attacks, upgrades and passive abilities.

cards.heading: Red fights the Process in real time and planned turns
cards.text: The player guides Red through Cloudbank from an isometric view. Her weapon, the Transistor, supplies the Functions used against the Process. Real-time movement and attacks can give way to a frozen planning mode, letting the player arrange a sequence before it plays out. Choosing what to equip changes the actions available during those encounters.

cards.heading: Functions serve as attacks, upgrades or passive powers
cards.text: Functions can be used in several ways. First, they can be equipped in one of four active skill slots. Second, they can be used as an upgrade to augment another equipped Function. Third, they can be equipped in a passive skill slot for a persistent effect during battle. For example, the Function Spark() may be used to fire an explosive attack, to split the effects of another Function, or to passively spawn Red's decoys. With a total of 16 Functions, there are many combinations, allowing for a great degree of customization to fit different play styles.

main.title: Watch Dogs
main.subtitle: Turn Chicago’s connected systems into tools for Aiden Pearce
main.summary: Watch Dogs is a 2014 action-adventure game developed by Ubisoft Montreal and published by Ubisoft. It is the first installment in the Watch Dogs series. The game is played from a third-person perspective, and its world is navigated on foot or by vehicle. Set within a fictionalized version of the Chicago metropolitan area in 2013, the single-player story follows grey hat hacker and vigilante Aiden Pearce's quest for revenge after the killing of his niece in a botched assassination attempt. An online multiplayer mode allows up to eight players to engage in cooperative and competitive gameplay.

cards.heading: Aiden Pearce pursues revenge in a connected Chicago
cards.text: Watch Dogs is a 2014 action-adventure game developed by Ubisoft Montreal and published by Ubisoft. It is the first installment in the Watch Dogs series. The game is played from a third-person perspective, and its world is navigated on foot or by vehicle. Set within a fictionalized version of the Chicago metropolitan area in 2013, the single-player story follows grey hat hacker and vigilante Aiden Pearce's quest for revenge after the killing of his niece in a botched assassination attempt. An online multiplayer mode allows up to eight players to engage in cooperative and competitive gameplay.

cards.heading: A smartphone opens different routes through the city
cards.text: Watch Dogs is an action-adventure game, played from a third-person view. The player controls hacker Aiden Pearce, who uses his smartphone to control trains and traffic lights, infiltrate security systems, jam cellphones, access pedestrians' private information, and empty their bank accounts. System hacking involves the solving of puzzles. The game is set in a fictionalized version of Chicago ("Windy City"), an open world environment which permits free-roaming. It has a day-night cycle and dynamic weather system, which changes the behavior of non-player characters (NPCs). For melee combat, Aiden has an extensible truncheon; other combat uses handguns, shotguns, sniper rifles, machine guns, and grenade launchers. There is a slow motion option for gunplay, and the player can use proximity IEDs, grenades, and electronic lures. Lethal and non-lethal mission approaches can be enacted.

cards.heading: Building Chicago and its hacking systems
cards.text: Development of the game began in 2009, and continued for over five years. Duties were shared by many of Ubisoft's studios worldwide, with more than a thousand people involved. The developers visited Chicago to conduct field research on the setting, and used regional language for authenticity. Hacking features were created in consultation with the cyber-security company Kaspersky Lab, and the in-game control system was based on SCADA. The score was composed by Brian Reitzell, who infused it with krautrock.

main.title: Mario Kart 8
main.subtitle: Race on walls and ceilings in the original Wii U Mario Kart
main.summary: Nintendo brings antigravity racing to Wii U, with Mario characters competing on walls, ceilings and familiar tracks.

cards.heading: Mario Kart arrives on Wii U
cards.text: Mario Kart 8 is Nintendo's kart racing game for Wii U, released in May 2014. Familiar Mario characters race on themed courses, collecting items that can change their chances of catching a rival or holding a lead. Its new antigravity sections take the track onto walls and ceilings. Single-player, local multiplayer and online modes carry the racing across Grand Prix events and other kinds of match.

cards.heading: Racing through antigravity sections
cards.text: Antigravity changes the route a course can follow. A wall or ceiling can become the road, so a race moves through a setting from several orientations while the player continues to steer, collect items and compete for position. The selected difficulty also changes the pace: higher settings make the racing faster. The combination gives familiar Mario Kart actions a different spatial setting, with the same contest for a good line and a useful power-up continuing through the change in orientation.

cards.heading: Expansions and the Switch Deluxe edition
cards.text: Nintendo expanded the Wii U release with additional courses and a new difficulty setting through paid and free downloadable content. Mario Kart 8 Deluxe brought the game to Switch in April 2017, including that material and revising the battle mode. Its later Booster Course Pass, released between March 2022 and November 2023, added another 48 tracks and eight characters. Keeping the editions together shows how the original Wii U game continued to develop on a second platform.

cards.heading: A game that continued across generations
cards.text: The original became Wii U's best-selling game, with 8.46 million copies sold. Deluxe also became the best-selling title on Switch, extending the same underlying game to a much larger audience. The releases shared the racing and presentation that reviewers had praised, while Deluxe addressed criticism of the original battle mode with a revised version. Mario Kart World followed as a launch title for Nintendo Switch 2 in 2025.
